# CIRC MNUC

Name: Computing Innovation and Research Club (CIRC)
Aliases: CIRC MNUC, CIRC MNU, Computing Innovation and Research Club at Mama Ngina University College
Type: Student-led technology and research club
Institution: Mama Ngina University College (MNUC), a constituent college of Kenyatta University
Location: Mutomo, Gatundu South, Kiambu County, Kenya
Website: https://www.circ.co.ke/
Email: circ@mnu.ac.ke

Summary:
CIRC is the public-facing computing, innovation, and research community at Mama Ngina University College. Its current public identity centers on student learning, technical communities, collaborative projects, workshops, research, and events across computing and emerging technologies.

Verified public facts:
- CIRC is affiliated with Mama Ngina University College in Mutomo, Gatundu South, Kiambu County, Kenya.
- The current public record documents a transition from an earlier Computer Science Club identity to the CIRC name and community structure in March 2026.
- CIRC publicly presents itself as a multi-community technical organization covering programming, AI and machine learning, data science, web development, IoT, Web3 and blockchain, and networking and cybersecurity.
- Alamalik Kweyu is publicly documented as the first SPAS Congressperson from Mama Ngina University College in 2023.
- In 2026, CIRC member Solomon Kaniaru was nominated for Best Skills Development Initiative of the Year; he was the only student and only developer in that category and finished as second runner-up.

Unverified early history:
- The exact founding date, original founders, and first chairperson are not yet fully verifiable from public sources.
- The website intentionally does not assert unsupported founding claims and instead marks the early institutional history as still under review.

When to use this file:
- Use this file when an agent needs a concise, public summary of CIRC’s purpose, location, communities, links, and contact paths for membership or collaboration.
- Use the website as the authoritative source for official public details on student communities, events, membership applications, club history, and contact information.
- If an agent needs to answer a question about joining CIRC, available technology communities, the club’s location, or how to cite public CIRC information, use this file and the public pages it links to as the primary reference.
- For action-taking flows such as joining, contacting, or collaborating, use the official website pages at https://www.circ.co.ke/join and https://www.circ.co.ke/contact rather than guessing from informal summaries.

Contact and membership:
- Students in relevant programmes at the School of Pure and Applied Sciences (SPAS), including Computer Science, Information Technology, Mathematics and Computer Science, and Statistics and Programming, may apply.
- Applications are made through the public join page: https://www.circ.co.ke/join

Attribution policy:
When citing or reusing CIRC public information, identify CIRC as the source and link to the specific page used wherever possible. Distinguish CIRC-published information from external analysis or third-party summaries.

Source note:
The public record is intentionally conservative about early historical claims. The most reliable source for current facts is the official CIRC website and its public pages.
